description: RISK R-B, STATED FIRST BECAUSE THE CLASS NAME INVERTS THE BEHAVIOUR: the prompt-mandated Java class for COTRN02C is TransactionViewController, but this program does not view - it ADDS. Two independent sources say so: app/cbl/COTRN02C.cbl:5 'Function    : Add a new Transaction to TRANSACT file', and the online-transaction table of README.md at L213-L231, whose CT02 row reads '| CT02 | COTRN02 | COTRN02C | Transaction Add |' and stands at README.md:224 - two lines below the 222 this file's authoring brief quotes, and cited as found rather than as briefed (practice B1). Rule R1 governs the resolution: the name comes from the prompt, the behaviour comes from the source. Practice B4 governs the disclosure, so the inversion is documented here and never silently corrected; the Agent Action Plan escalates it for explicit user confirmation, and the mirror image is parity/COTRN01C, whose program genuinely views. No case in this folder is downgraded to read-only to match the name - the EXEC CICS WRITE at :713 is pinned at its full 350 bytes by case19 and case20. WHAT THIS CASE DRIVES: the second arm of VALIDATE-INPUT-KEY-FIELDS, and then the WHEN OTHER arm of READ-CCXREF-FILE - the one cross-reference outcome no other case in this folder reaches. The path is REENTER, so CDEMO-PGM-CONTEXT arrives at '1', the NOT CDEMO-PGM-REENTER test at :120 is false and :132 performs RECEIVE-TRNADD-SCREEN; EIBAID is DFHENTER, so the ordered EVALUATE at :133-152 takes its first arm at :134-135 and performs PROCESS-ENTER-KEY. Inside VALIDATE-INPUT-KEY-FIELDS the EVALUATE TRUE at :195 finds ACTIDINI at spaces, so the :196 guard - the abbreviated combined relation NOT = SPACES AND LOW-VALUES, which a blank field satisfies neither half of - is false, and CARDNINI holding sixteen digits satisfies the :210 guard. The COBOL class test at :211 passes because every character is a digit; FUNCTION NUMVAL at :218-219 converts the image into WS-CARD-NUM-N PIC 9(16); :220-221 is one statement with two receivers, so the renormalised sixteen zero-padded digits are moved into both XREF-CARD-NUM and back over the input item the operator typed into - legal and intended, because COTRN2AO REDEFINES COTRN2AI - and :222 performs the read. THE THREE ARMS OF READ-CCXREF-FILE AND WHO OWNS EACH: the paragraph at :609-637 issues EXEC CICS READ DATASET(WS-CCXREF-FILE) RIDFLD(XREF-CARD-NUM), which is the CCXREF base cluster keyed on the card number, and then EVALUATEs WS-RESP-CD in source order. DFHRESP(NORMAL) at :622-623 is CONTINUE and is owned by case03, which reaches this same arm through CDEMO-CT02-TRN-SELECTED at :124-127 and whose key resolves against the seeded base, so validation proceeds to the data fields. DFHRESP(NOTFND) at :624-629 reports 'Card Number NOT found...' with the cursor on the card field and emits NO diagnostic; it is owned by case11, whose key is absent from the fixture. WHEN OTHER at :630-636 is this case, and gate G30 is satisfied by its position: it is written last and is reached only when neither named response matches. With case09 and case10 taking the not-found and unexpected halves of the alternate-index read at :576-604, and the normal half of that read exercised by case06 and by case13 onward, the six cross-reference outcomes of this program are now exhausted (gate G47). THE INJECTED RESPONSE, NAMED AND TRACED (practice B8): no arrangement of seeded rows can reach this arm, because the source does not enumerate the condition it stands for - so the case declares a forced outcome for the keyed read, and the harness fails the run if a declared outcome is left unconsumed rather than letting the ordinary path pass while the case claims otherwise. The declared outcome is OTHER on the read operation; both cross-reference finders share that single key because the EVALUATE TRUE at :195 takes exactly one arm, so one run performs exactly one of the two reads and the declaration cannot be ambiguous. It resolves to CardXrefRepository.ReadResult.other over the CCXREF base, and that factory fixes the pair the program displays: RESP is DFHRESP(NOTOPEN), decimal 19 - neither DFHRESP(NORMAL), which is 0, nor DFHRESP(NOTFND), which is 13 - and RESP2 is 0, the not-applicable value reported for a condition carrying no reason code. NOTOPEN is the closest true analogue of a dataset the access layer could not reach, which is precisely what an unexpected response means here. The pair is named in this prose rather than restated in the forced outcome's own resp and resp2 members, which stay unstated: on this path the factory takes no response argument, so a number written there would claim an influence the case does not have (practice B1). THE DIAGNOSTIC, DERIVED FROM ITS PICTURE CLAUSE (practices B8 and B11): :631 is DISPLAY 'RESP:' WS-RESP-CD 'REAS:' WS-REAS-CD, and app/cbl/COTRN02C.cbl:47-48 declares both operands PIC S9(09) COMP VALUE ZEROS. DISPLAY concatenates its operands at their declared widths and inserts no separator, so each nine-digit-position receiver renders as nine characters and the line is 5 + 9 + 5 + 9 = 28 characters exactly: 'RESP:' then 000000019 then 'REAS:' then 000000000. The width comes from the picture clause rather than from a guess, and the rendering is identical in form and in value to case10's, because :598 and :631 are byte-identical statements reached with the same forced response - only the literal that follows differs. This is the ONLY one of the three cross-reference arms that emits a diagnostic: :622 continues silently, and :624-629 rejects without displaying, which case11 pins as the non-event it is. FOUR DISTINCT 'UNABLE TO' LITERALS, AND WHY THIS ONE: the program carries five byte-identical DISPLAY statements, at :598, :631, :662, :691 and :743, and the literals that follow them are NOT interchangeable. :600 in READ-CXACAIX-FILE says 'Unable to lookup Acct in XREF AIX file...'; :633 here says 'Unable to lookup Card # in XREF file...'; :664 in STARTBR-TRANSACT-FILE and :693 in READPREV-TRANSACT-FILE both say 'Unable to lookup Transaction...'; and :745 in WRITE-TRANSACT-FILE says 'Unable to Add Transaction...'. This case carries the :633 literal byte for byte - the space before the number sign, 'XREF file' where the alternate-index sibling says 'XREF AIX file', and the three trailing full stops. Crossing any two of them would leave the arm correctly driven and the expectation quietly wrong, which is the failure this paragraph exists to prevent. WHY THE ACCOUNT FIELD IS STILL BLANK: SEND-TRNADD-SCREEN at :516-534 ends with EXEC CICS RETURN TRANSID(WS-TRANID) COMMAREA(CARDDEMO-COMMAREA), which terminates the CICS task. The PERFORM at :636 therefore never returns, so :223 - MOVE XREF-ACCT-ID TO ACTIDINI - is never executed and VALIDATE-INPUT-DATA-FIELDS at :235-437 never runs at all. ACTIDINO is consequently the eleven spaces that arrived, unchanged, and no data-field text appears: there is no empty-field message and no 'Confirm to add this transaction...' prompt. CARDNINO is the sixteen zero-padded digits :221 wrote back over the input item. The cursor is CARDNINL, the COMP PIC S9(4) length item :635 moved -1 into; a length item is validation metadata rather than a payload member, so it is recorded as the response's cursor field and never as a screen field. ERRMSGO is WS-MESSAGE after :520 moves a PIC X(80) field into a PIC X(78) receiver, left justified and space padded, so the two message channels differ by exactly the two bytes COBOL loses on the right (rule R5). The header six come from POPULATE-HEADER-INFO at :552-571 against the clock pinned to 2022-07-19T23:12:34 - the single instant all twenty cases in this folder share, so the run is deterministic in any timezone (practice B7): 'CT02' from WS-TRANID, 'COTRN02C' from WS-PGMNAME, the two titles from app/cpy/COTTL01Y.cpy, 07/19/22 as MM/DD/YY and 23:12:34 as HH:MM:SS. ERRMSGC stays at the default colour, because DFHGREEN is moved only on the successful-write arm at :727. THE MESSAGE CHANNELS, RECONCILED WITH THE FROZEN CONTRACT (practice B4): the authoring brief asks for an ordered pair - the diagnostic first, then the screen message - and that is exactly the order asserted. It is expressed as three entries rather than two because the screen message is reported on both of its declared widths: ParityCase.MessageChannel names WS_MESSAGE_80 for the PIC X(80) working-storage field and SCREEN_ERRMSG_78 for the PIC X(78) screen field, and COTRN02CParityTest records DISPLAY lines first and then both message channels whenever a screen was sent. On that mechanical split the frozen wire contract wins, as the brief itself directs; the logical ordering it requires is unchanged, and reporting only one width would make the two-byte loss at :520 unobservable. A NORMAL RETURN, NOT AN EXCEPTION (gate G47): CardXrefRepository reports this condition as a discriminated outcome carrying a common.FileStatus value together with the CICS response pair, and never abends on the caller's behalf. COTRN02C contains ZERO CALL 'CEE3ABD' anywhere in its 783 lines, so even an unexpected response is an ordinary return that paints a screen and hands the terminal back: expectedReturnCode is 0, nothing is thrown, and there is no non-zero exit to assert. Turning this arm into an exception or into a failing exit status is the likeliest divergence, so the expectation states the opposite explicitly. Gate G35 is therefore deliberately NOT asserted, and neither is G32 - this program contains no GO TO - nor G39, which has no pagination loop to measure, nor G43, which has no 9300-CHECK-CHANGE-IN-REC to preserve. There is no G40 either: the task returns to itself pseudo-conversationally rather than transferring, so the response names COTRN02C and the termination is RETURN_TRANSID. All 22 fields of the 218-byte communication area are pinned and none omitted, because the conversation state travels in the payload rather than in a server-side session (rule R6, gate G37) and an unpinned field is a field nobody has checked; the REENTER half of gate G38 is exercised here with the error flag raised and the cursor set. THE SEED, AND WHAT IS DELIBERATELY NOT SEEDED: CCXREF is seeded from five rows of the cardxref.txt fixture exactly as they ship, 36 bytes wide, and is deliberately NOT pre-padded - app/cpy/CVACT03Y.cpy declares CARD-XREF-RECORD as XREF-CARD-NUM PIC X(16) plus XREF-CUST-ID PIC 9(09) plus XREF-ACCT-ID PIC 9(11) plus FILLER PIC X(14), which sums 16 + 9 + 11 + 14 = 50, and the fixture omits that trailing FILLER, so the CARDXREF_FILLER_PAD_36_TO_50 normalisation declared below supplies the fourteen spaces once, at seed time, and parity/FieldDiffer is the sole owner of that repair (gate G16, risk R-F). The key this case sends, 0500024453765740, is row 0 of that fixture and DOES exist in the seeded base: the read fails anyway, which is the substance of the arm - the condition is that the dataset could not be reached, not that the key was missing, and that is exactly what separates this case from case11's not-found. CXACAIX is not seeded as a dataset of its own, because app/csd/CARDDEMO.CSD defines it as a PATH over this same CCXREF base: one repository per base plus a finder for the alternate key serves both access paths and no second table exists (gate G45), and this case never performs that read at all. Every dataset is addressed by its application.yml binding key rather than by name, so no fully qualified mainframe dataset name appears anywhere in this file (gate G46); no tenth fixture is named, the set being closed at the nine derived from app/data/ASCII; and the code page is stated as US-ASCII rather than left to a platform default (practice B8). Three TRANSACT rows are declared inline because no ASCII fixture ships for that master - it is populated online, not loaded - each 350 bytes summed from app/cpy/CVTRA05Y.cpy, and all three stand byte-identical on the final-state channel: the backward browse at :642-706 and the WRITE at :713 are never reached, and TRANSACT has no REWRITE and no DELETE anywhere in the codebase, so expectedWrites is empty and the master still holds exactly three rows of exactly 350 bytes. ACCTDAT IS A DEAD DECLARATION, PRESERVED AND NOT TIDIED (practice B5): WS-ACCTDAT-FILE PIC X(08) VALUE 'ACCTDAT ' is declared at :40 and COPY CVACT01Y at :89, and neither is referenced anywhere in the program - no DATASET operand names WS-ACCTDAT-FILE and no field of ACCOUNT-RECORD is ever moved - so the account master is a dead name and its copybook a dead include. No ACCTDAT input is declared here and no ACCTDAT row appears in any expectation in this folder, because seeding a master the program never opens would assert a read that does not exist. The arm under test is preserved with the same discipline: the DISPLAY comes FIRST and is not suppressed as noise, the literal keeps its wording and its ellipsis, and -1 goes only to the card field's length item and nowhere else. ENDBR at :704-706 is a bare EXEC CICS ENDBR with no RESP operand and no EVALUATE, so it has no unexpected-response arm and is given no error expectation here or anywhere. CASE ALLOCATION, RECONCILED IN THE OPEN (practice B4): this file's authoring brief placed the three cross-reference base outcomes at case12, case13 and case14. As built, the folder places them at case03, case11 and here, while case12 drives the card-number class test and case13 the positional amount check - so the brief's sibling map is restated above as verified rather than as assumed. The slot this case now occupies previously held the positional origination-date check at :353-366, which was the only cross-reference arm-free case in the folder and, unlike the WHEN OTHER arm at :630-636, was already driven independently by the module's own unit test for TransactionViewController. Reassigning the slot therefore adds the one cross-reference outcome that no case reached while leaving no branch undriven, and the exchange is recorded here rather than made silently. BASELINE PROVENANCE (practice B12): every expected value here is STATICALLY DERIVED - by structured reading of MAIN-PARA, PROCESS-ENTER-KEY, VALIDATE-INPUT-KEY-FIELDS, READ-CCXREF-FILE, SEND-TRNADD-SCREEN and POPULATE-HEADER-INFO, cross-checked against the copybook byte layouts (app/cpy/COCOM01Y.cpy as 160 bytes and the CDEMO-CT02-INFO extension at :72-80 as 16 + 16 + 8 + 1 + 1 + 16 = 58, so the passed area is 218; app/cpy/CVTRA05Y.cpy 350; app/cpy/CVACT03Y.cpy 50), against the PIC S9(09) COMP declarations at :47-48 that fix the diagnostic's width, against the symbolic-map widths of app/cpy-bms/COTRN02.CPY (21 payload input items summing to 396, a 555-byte group image, ACTIDINI PIC X(11), CARDNINI PIC X(16), ERRMSGO PIC X(78), and the length, flag and attribute items that are metadata and never payload), and against the real bytes of app/data/ASCII. It was NEVER captured from a live COBOL execution: running the legacy programs is empirically impossible in this environment, which Agent Action Plan section 0.7.6 establishes with eight independently verified blockers - among them a compiler whose indexed-file handler is disabled, no Language Environment CEE service behind CSUTLDTC, no CICS emulator, and the absence of the IBM-supplied DFHAID and DFHBMSCA copybooks this program copies at :92-93 - and the change of provenance is escalated as risk R-A rather than absorbed silently. The DFHENTER mnemonic is consequently declared through common.CicsAid, which is this migration's single reproduction of the absent DFHAID (risk R-D). NO USER RULES EXIST: review_rules returns exactly one line, 'No user rules provided.', and that line is the whole document, so no user rule forces this file into scope and none constrains how it is written. The absence is stated explicitly and is not treated as permission to lower the bar: the standard held here is the Agent Action Plan section 0.10.2 enterprise practices, cited by name where they bite - B1 (every literal derived and verified, no placeholder anywhere), B3 (app/cbl, app/cpy, app/cpy-bms, app/bms, app/csd and app/data are read-only and were not touched), B4 (the R-B inversion, the channel split and the slot reassignment all disclosed), B5 (the dead declarations and the arm preserved exactly), B7 (a pinned clock), B8 (the injected response named, the diagnostic's derivation shown, binding keys not dataset names, US-ASCII named), B11 (every width taken from a picture clause) and B12 (the provenance statement above). GATES DISCHARGED: G15 (one of exactly twenty cases in parity/COTRN02C), G16, G18 (the diff count must be zero, per module rather than per build), G30, G37, G38, G45, G46, G47 and G51 - the controller is driven as a plain object, constructed and called directly, with no MockMvc, no servlet container, no HTTP and no JobLauncher in the path.
